points.point: Diesel-off operation is not technically established: the main design holds the grid with no diesel for 7,302 h/yr at 0.251 USD/kWh, but with one diesel always on its LCOE becomes 0.414 USD/kWh and the optimum falls to 1,500 kWp/1,000 kWh; frequency/voltage control, grid-forming inverters and protection are excluded, so a reserve requirement could erase the claimed -29.1% saving.

The demand basis is unresolved: annual demand of 9,568,110 kWh/yr and peak of 1,422 kW are derived from Hiron 2021, yet the study flags 7 of 24 hourly rows failing energy balance and load totals of 2.648e+07 vs 2.621e+04 kWh; no metered PLN load series or reconciled hourly profile is provided before sizing a 19,000 kWh battery.
points.addressed_in: The published study we used: Hiron 2021 (Energies 14, 8311)

points.point: Up-front capital of 14,287,750 USD is exactly 7,250 x 1,119 plus 19,000 x 300 plus 4,750 x 100 USD, with no identifiable allowance for island shipping, local labour, land, grid-integration/protection upgrades, development, taxes or contingency; the 1,119 USD/kWp value is also a 2022 paper value used in a stated 2025 currency-year model without shown escalation.

Battery economics rest on assumed inputs: 300 USD/kWh, 100 USD/kW and a 12 yr life remain assumed after a 192 USD/kWh source was rejected, while the duty is 249 full cycles/yr at 0.90 round-trip efficiency and there is no capacity-fade, throughput-warranty or salt-air degradation model beyond a fixed replacement rule within the 20 yr project.

The diesel baseline is largely assumed: fuel at 0.848485 USD/L comes from 14,000 IDR/L in a generic document plus an assumed 16,500 IDR/USD exchange rate rather than a Karimunjawa delivered price; the fuel-curve intercept 0.08 L/h/kW-rated, slope 0.25 L/kWh and diesel O&M 0.03 USD/kWh are assumed, and 217 diesel starts/yr carry no stated start, minimum-run or overhaul cost.

The land-fit claim is too tight to bank: the design needs 8.3 ha from about 9.0 ha set aside, with the largest fitting PV stated as 7,830 kWp, using a US median density of 0.87 MWdc/ha, while ownership, permits, environmental review, layout, shading, soil and construction access remain outside the study.

The investment case is incomplete: discount rate is an assumed 8% real while NPC of 23,591,478 USD and LCOE of 0.251 USD/kWh are presented, but financing terms, tariffs, subsidies, counterparty and who pays the 14,287,750 USD up-front cost are excluded; discount sensitivity is only +/-20%.

There is no bankable solar-yield or reliability case: satellite GHI spans 1,731 to 2,049 kWh/m2/yr, an 18.4% spread, and weather-case LCOE spans 0.215 to 0.251 USD/kWh, but there is no on-site measurement, P50/P90 yield, multi-year worst-period test, PV degradation or soiling allowance behind the reported 0 kWh/yr unserved energy.

Diesel fleet rating is contradictory and material: the study uses 2 x 1,800 kW although Hiron also prints 2 x 2,700 kW; with 2,700 kW units diesel-only LCOE becomes 0.410 USD/kWh, least-cost LCOE 0.260 USD/kWh and the reserve-case optimum falls to 750 kWp/0 kWh, so actual nameplate rating, unit condition and maintenance capability at the 1,422 kW peak need field verification.

The expansion path is undefined: the growth case optimum is 8,500 kWp/22,000 kWh at 0.249 USD/kWh, above the stated 7,830 kWp land cap, but the growth rate, target year, tourist-season and growth load shapes, staging plan and treatment of new loads such as electric boats are not specified enough to reserve land or stage procurement.
